title: Label coverage
feed: ROPA Record, row Discovery scan check
context: At LearnTech, data discovery and labelling run on Microsoft Purview Information Protection with DSPM, named here only for context. DataSentry is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All repository data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst checks a RoPA entry against the data catalogue's discovery scan before the DPO approves it: an owner's description names the systems they know, and the scan finds the copies they forgot.
owner: Your RoPA entry and data-flow map are drawn from the Regional EdTech Manager's description, and a description misses copies. Before the entry goes to the DPO, check LearnTech's data catalogue: where has the latest discovery scan found the corporate LMS's personal data, is each place on your map, and is each labelled as it should be? Capture what you find, so the DPO can rely on it without opening the console.
rules: Each organisation keeps a RoPA entry for every processing activity (GDPR Art.30) … Its data-flow map shows where the personal data is collected, the systems that hold it, every transfer and where it is deleted, with the system names of the asset register. … A transfer is any movement of personal data out of that country, including when people in another country view it or download it remotely.
What that means for a repository

A repository is on the map when a flow of your DFM puts the activity's data in that repository's system, in that repository's country. A system on the map in one country does not cover its copy in another.

Processor: processes personal data on behalf of a controller, only on the controller's documented instructions and for the controller's purposes … An organisation that uses the personal data for a purpose of its own becomes a controller for that purpose, and records it as a separate processing activity.

Owner classifies: the asset owner recorded in the Information Asset Register is accountable for classification. Copies, extracts, screenshots and reports inherit the classification of the source. A repository therefore carries the label the Classification register gives its system.
Tier 3 Confidential: visible label (header+footer+metadata); MIP/DLP label mandatory. Tier 4 Restricted: visible label on every page/screen; watermark with user ID; DLP block rules.

parts.title: Where the activity's personal data sits
parts.ask: Find every repository where the scan found personal data of the corporate LMS activity, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Discovery scans. Use two filters together: one for the activity, one for what the scan found. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Is each one on your data-flow map?
parts.ask: For each repository you captured, decide whether your DFM accounts for it.
parts.where: Discovery scans gives each repository's System and Country. DFM, in this step's hand-in on the desk, gives each flow's line and its System: close this window to read it, and open it again from Systems. The rules you apply says when a repository is on the map.

parts.title: Is each one labelled as it should be?
parts.ask: For each repository you captured, compare the label applied with the label its system should carry.
parts.where: Discovery scans shows each repository's System and Label applied. Classification register gives each system's label. BKB-STD-001 is in The rules you apply.

parts.title: Policies that only watch
parts.ask: BKB-STD-001 Section 6 asks for DLP block rules on Tier 4 data. Find every policy for LearnTech's Tier 4 label that does not block, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Policies. Classification register says which label is Tier 4; the Policies screen says what each Mode does. Use two filters together.

parts.title: What the DPO is asked to approve
parts.ask: For each repository not on your map, decide what the DPO should be asked to approve.
parts.where: Catalogue gives each repository's registered purpose: compare it with the client's purposes in your ROPA, in this step's hand-in. Discovery scans gives its Country. BKB-POL-017 Sections 3.1 and 3.2 are in The rules you apply.
